clue.text: One checking road crime, special vigour limiting breaking of code (8, two words)

indicators.note: a code that is broken is cracked open and its letters rearranged
to limit something is to hem it in, so the outer word closes around the inner one

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for special
pep is energy or vigour
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A traffic officer's energy is spent catching motorists who break the highway code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking of code' reads like breaking the highway code, but it tells you to scramble the word code before the outer pieces close round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed cop is a police officer who catches motorists exceeding limits, a traffic offence.

clue.text: Junk, cold, dumped in sink

indicators.note: something dumped in a place ends up inside it

blocks.note: to sag is to sink
C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Rubbish has been left cold in the kitchen basin.
explanation.walkthrough: Junk looks like rubbish but is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scag and junk are both slang terms for heroin among drug users.

clue.text: Viewdata system was still mostly in programming language

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the last letter is lost
in places the shortened word inside the other

blocks.note: PL, as in PL/1, stands for programming language
to have rested is to have been still

explanation.surface: An old information service sat mostly idle inside a piece of software.
explanation.walkthrough: Prestel was the British Post Office's pioneering viewdata service, sending text pages over phone lines to TV screens.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestel was a proprietary name for a videotex service delivering text pages by telephone to televisions.

clue.text: Muffs organ and delays involving consequence (12, two words)

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the delays enclose the next item

blocks.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
to defer is to delay
an end is an outcome or consequence

explanation.surface: A part of the body and delays bring consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear defenders, or ear muffs, are padded covers protecting the hearing from loud noise.

clue.text: Crack that's devoid of extremes? It was a mild oath

indicators.note: lacking its extremes means the first and last letters are gone

blocks.note: to crack a cipher is to decode it

explanation.surface: A gentle joke or remark without excess once passed for a soft curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecod is an archaic exclamation, a softened 'by God', so 'it was' marks it as old.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecod was an old interjection used as a minced, mild form of swearing by God.

clue.text: Ticked off flower without tincture?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named part is removed

blocks.note: the orchid is a flower
or is gold, a heraldic tincture

explanation.surface: Someone scolded a bloom for lacking colour.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry the tinctures are the colours and metals, and or is gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold, so it means told off or reprimanded.

clue.text: Dancing in pub reel, not yet ready to get hitched

definitions.text: not yet ready to get hitched

indicators.note: dancing letters jump about and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Young people dance a reel in the pub, too young to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Prenubile means before the age of marriageability, so too young to wed.

clue.text: Swells kicked the bucket after end of celebration

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept here

blocks.note: the final letter of celebration
ob. (obiit) is the Latin abbreviation for died, found on gravestones; pluralised to fit the plural swells

explanation.surface: Grand party guests drop dead once the festivities finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the died abbreviation behind the N. OB stands for obiit, 'he or she died'; Azed takes it in the plural to match the swells, giving N + OBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobs and swells are both old slang for wealthy, upper-class or fashionable people.

clue.text: Passing remark, one taking effect in blame around court (12, two words)

indicators.note: in puts the first item inside the word for blame
around has the word for blame wrap the court too

blocks.note: odium is blame or opprobrium
something that takes effect bites, so it is a biter
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A judge's offhand comment, criticised in court once it takes effect.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate pieces sit inside the word for blame at different points. 'One taking effect' is one that bites, as a measure bites when it starts to work.
explanation.definitionFit: An obiter dictum is an incidental remark, especially a judge's comment not essential to the ruling.

clue.text: Something for treating complexion to put in receptacle

indicators.note: put in a receptacle means placed inside it

blocks.note: a box is a receptacle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A skin cream is placed in a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Botox is a trade name for botulinum toxin, injected to smooth wrinkles in the skin.

clue.text: Like a caveman, tumbling asleep if old

indicators.note: tumbling letters fall over and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an is an archaic word for if

explanation.surface: A primitive man drops off to sleep, if the old stories are true.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelaean means cave-dwelling or relating to caves, from the Greek for cave.

clue.text: Expert creating flaw

blocks.note: first meaning: highly skilled
second meaning: a split or fissure in something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Creating' only joins the two meanings, the adjective and the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means first-rate and skilled; as a noun it is a fracture or defect.

clue.text: Jazz type making poet dance switching parts (7, two words)

indicators.note: switching parts means the opening sounds of the two words change places

blocks.note: a bard is a poet and a hop is an informal dance; their opening sounds then trade places

explanation.surface: A style of jazz inspires a poet to get up and dance.
explanation.walkthrough: BARD HOP with its initial letters swapped becomes HARD BOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard bop is a 1950s development of bebop jazz, influenced by blues and gospel.

clue.text: A tide rose, i.e. somehow about right, indicating heavenly body

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some unspecified order
about places the rearranged letters around another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A rising tide seems to point to something in the heavens, as tides follow the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The tide image suggests the moon, but the heavenly body is a rarer thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosiderite is an iron meteorite, a body that falls to earth from the sky.

clue.text: Old vessels? One experienced in military service in Spanish parliament

indicators.note: in places the veteran inside the parliament

blocks.note: the Cortes is the Spanish parliament
a vet, short for veteran, has served in the forces

explanation.surface: Old soldiers sit in the Spanish chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: corvettes were once sailing warships, and still exist as small escort ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Corvettes were small, flush-decked sailing warships of the age of sail, later light escort ships.

clue.text: Smear in meat stew, French, not English

indicators.note: not here means leaving out the named letter

blocks.note: a daube is a French braised meat stew
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A French casserole leaves a stain on the tablecloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To daub is to smear or coat roughly with a sticky substance like paint or plaster.

clue.text: It involves take-offs and landings, many returning

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: lots means many

explanation.surface: An airfield handles a great number of departures and arrivals.
explanation.walkthrough: STOL stands for short take-off and landing; the many movements of such aircraft make the whole clue a description too.
explanation.definitionFit: STOL is an aviation acronym for aircraft designed for short take-off and landing runs.

clue.text: Jurassic creature, sort e.g. roaming round USA, wild

indicators.note: roaming letters wander out of their places into a fresh order
round puts the first rearranged group around the second
wild letters are untamed and come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dinosaur of some kind roams wild across America.
explanation.definitionFit: The stegosaur is a plated herbivorous dinosaur that lived in the Jurassic period.

clue.text: Electrician consumes rotten matter, ay lost, in temporary part of vessel (8, two words)

indicators.note: to consume is to take inside, so the electrician swallows the matter
lost means the named letters are taken away

blocks.note: sparks is slang for an electrician
decay is rotten matter
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: An electrician finds rot aboard and fixes something temporary on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparks, or spark, is slang for an electrician or a ship's radio officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar deck is a light upper deck on a ship, originally a temporary deck laid over spars.

clue.text: One's bowed, displaying dowager hump in part

indicators.note: displaying means the phrase shows the answer within its letters

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: An elderly lady bends over, showing a stooped back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's bowed' looks like a person stooping, but it is a stringed instrument played with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: The erhu is a two-stringed Chinese fiddle played with a bow drawn between its strings.

clue.text: Tramp perished in wartime service

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for died inside the service

blocks.note: HO, 'hostilities only', described wartime enlistment for the duration
ob. (obiit) is the Latin abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A wandering vagrant died while serving in the war.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is an itinerant worker or homeless vagrant, the same as a tramp.

clue.text: Ballot-box information twice yielding names to press

indicators.note: yielding names means giving up the letter for name, here on two occasions

blocks.note: votes are cast into a ballot urn
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Electoral data, read out twice, gives the names needed to lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: URN + GEN loses both its Ns (N = name). Gen is British slang for the facts on something.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge or press someone is to push them strongly towards an action.

clue.text: Sound made by Scotsman, exceedingly jolly

indicators.note: a sound made by someone is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman
oh so means very or exceedingly

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's cry sounds exceedingly cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, Jock plus oh so gives the Italian musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Giocoso is an Italian musical direction meaning playful or merry, to be performed jokingly.

clue.text: Indicating port side, outer bits cut from whale bone

indicators.note: cutting the outer bits trims off the first and last letters

blocks.note: baleen is the horny plate in a whale's mouth, often called whalebone

explanation.surface: A ship's left side is marked, as someone trims a whale's bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whale bone' is one idea, baleen, rather than two words to clip.
explanation.definitionFit: Alee means on or toward the sheltered side of a ship, away from the wind, a nautical direction.

clue.text: Charm I discerned in African chieftain

indicators.note: something discerned in another is seen sitting inside it

blocks.note: an oba is a hereditary chief in West Africa
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tribal leader is credited with personal charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: An oba is a ruler among the Yoruba and Edo peoples of Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Obia, or obeah, is West Indian sorcery, and an obia can be a fetish or magic charm.

clue.text: Bear black tuber

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
aloo is the Indian word for potato, a tuber

explanation.surface: A black potato is on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Baloo is a Hindi word for a bear, also the name of the bear in The Jungle Book.

clue.text: Dance round baron, brave one in activity involving boxers?

indicators.note: round says the dance wraps around the next item

blocks.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
B is the abbreviation for baron
the lion is proverbially brave

explanation.surface: A dance swirls around a nobleman before a contest between boxers.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxers suggests the ring, but the Boxers were a Chinese secret society whose uprising of 1899–1901 is known as the Boxer Rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boxer Rebellion was a revolt in China, so an uprising is literally an activity of Boxers.

clue.text: Trouble going after depth in border

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for depth
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Difficulties arise from how deep a frame or margin is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going after' places the trouble behind the depth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower part of a room's wall, often marked off as a decorative band or border.

clue.text: Crab larva, ordinary, found among maize

indicators.note: found among means sitting inside the other

blocks.note: Zea is the botanical genus of maize
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A tiny crab grub is discovered in a field of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoea is the early free-swimming larval stage of crabs and other decapod crustaceans.

clue.text: Try on old-fashioned skirt

blocks.note: a go is a try or attempt
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A person tries on an outdated skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try on' looks like fitting clothes, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A gore is a tapering panel of a skirt, and in old usage meant the skirt itself.

clue.text: Serving girl, fresh up, taking recipe in

indicators.note: up in a down entry means read from bottom to top
taking in means enclosing the other piece

blocks.note: fresh means new
R, from Latin recipe 'take', heads prescriptions

explanation.surface: A fresh young waitress takes in a new recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, so a woman serving in the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrens were women serving in the Royal Navy's women's service, hence a serving girl.

clue.text: Picked for office tomorrow? Almost, in a way, as power source

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in a way hints the word is rendered after a fashion, not in its true order

blocks.note: elect is the adjective for one chosen but not yet installed, as in president-elect
taken as written, to be shortened and rearranged

explanation.surface: A candidate elected tomorrow, or nearly, takes office as a source of power.
explanation.definitionFit: An electromotor is an electric motor, a machine that turns electrical energy into motive power.

clue.text: Sheep occupying centre in procession

indicators.note: something occupying a space sits inside it

blocks.note: the core is the centre
a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: Sheep fill the middle of a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Teg is a farming word for a yearling sheep, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a solemn procession, especially of mourners following a funeral.

clue.text: Doctor given exercise for cavity

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes exercise for a dental cavity.
explanation.walkthrough: The tooth reading of cavity is the trap; this cavity is in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A druse is a rock cavity lined with crystals, a geological term.

clue.text: Digger on ship a short distance from India

blocks.note: a ko is a Maori digging stick
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A labourer aboard a vessel lies not far off the Indian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the digger before the ship in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A koss, or kos, is an Indian unit of distance of about two miles, a modest span.

clue.text: Fish twice interspersed with English marine slug (8, two words)

indicators.note: interspersed means dotted through, so the extra letters go inside at points

blocks.note: the salmon is a fish
gives no letters itself: it says the English letter is used two times
E for English, taken two times

explanation.surface: Fish caught twice near English shores turn out to be sea slugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Twice tells you to use E two times, each one dropped into a different gap of the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea lemon is a yellowish nudibranch, a kind of shell-less sea slug.
